A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TMCL research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR-100 continual-learning experiments, downstream transfer results, ablations and ten-session results in the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds ImageNet-100 evaluation, label-noise experiments and expanded ResNet comparisons.

M1.justification: The procedure remains sparse-label OPL training of affine modulations over frozen feedforward weights, followed by view- and modulation-invariant consolidation. The architecture details and Appendix C pseudocode retain the same components and training sequence. The rewritten mathematical explanation does not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: v2 adds ImageNet-100 continual learning and a CIFAR-100 scenario with corrupted supervision. These substantially broaden the evaluated data and learning conditions. CIFAR-100 and the nine downstream transfer datasets from v1 are retained.

E2.justification: The five-session ConViT comparison removes CaSSLe variants previously reported in v1 Table 2. v2 Table 6 expands ResNet comparisons with CLS-ER and literature-adapted ER, DER, LUMP, Less-Forget and POD results. The literature CaSSLe/PNR results moved into Table 6 are retained comparisons, not new additions.

E3.justification: Added protocols include random replacement of 30%, 50%, 90% and 99% of labels, ResNet evaluation with 10% labels, and ImageNet class splits varying across seeds. Appendix A specifies 200 ImageNet pretraining epochs, although Section 4 still gives 250 generally. Five-session and ablation reporting drops kNN in favor of linear readout; the existing CIFAR training recipe and ten-session protocol remain.

E4.justification: v2 adds a substantial label-noise robustness study, extends the trained/untrained/random modulation and OPL-versus-BCE ablations to ImageNet, and reports BCE convergence diagnostics. ResNet analysis also expands to sparse supervision. The existing MI-strength, CDNV and predictor/stop-gradient analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Table 1 specifies three seeds for ImageNet and four for CIFAR, adding a different run-count specification without establishing any reduction in existing experiments. Mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting and the CDNV minimum/maximum shading remain. The checklist's blanket claim of four seeds conflicts with the ImageNet table.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive ImageNet, label-noise and ResNet results while removing several CIFAR baseline entries and kNN columns. For example, newly reported ImageNet accuracy with 1% labels is 62.0 ± 0.2 for VI+MI versus 59.7 ± 0.3 for VI. A retained CIFAR result also changes: VI+SI(PNR)+SupCon with 1% labels changes from 60.2 ± 0.1 to 60.1 ± 0.3. Transfer, ten-session and backward/forward-transfer table values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3 adds class-center definitions and explicit orthogonality/invariance conditions with a short sufficiency argument, elaborated in Appendix D. This provides limited additional mathematical reasoning rather than a theorem framework. The OPL, transfer and CDNV definitions remain, while v1's explicit Barlow Twins and multiview-loss formulas are omitted.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain the same central contributions: consolidating sparse supervision through top-down modulations, improving continual and transfer learning, and balancing stability with plasticity. The added experiments support these claims without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations for label-noise robustness, incomplete BCE collapse on ImageNet and BatchNorm-related interference in ResNets. Appendix D explicitly qualifies full mutual orthogonality as an ideal condition that the implemented continual procedure cannot rigorously guarantee. These additions materially expand the mechanism and applicability discussion.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly reports code availability and supplies a repository address; Appendix H identifies NVIDIA DALI for ImageNet loading and augmentation. Most hyperparameters, hardware information and pseudocode are retained. Conversely, omission of the explicit multiview Barlow Twins formula removes some implementation guidance available in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds ImageNet and AdamW references and removes the NMDA-spike citation group and the multiview-pretraining reference accompanying the deleted explanation. The principal positioning relative to biological learning, modulation methods and continual-learning approaches remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 3 is substantially rewritten around class-center objectives and explicit VI/MI formulations, replacing the earlier biological-gain exposition and taxonomy-led explanation. The experimental narrative is reorganized and expanded, a dedicated explanatory appendix is added, and a conference checklist is inserted. Much of the abstract and discussion remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 redraws Figure 2, adds a graphical legend to Figure 1, rearranges Figure 3 and adopts a substantially different conference layout. It removes the invariance-taxonomy table, rebuilds the main comparison table, separates architectural and modulation ablations, and adds noise and expanded ResNet tables. Several retained displays are relocated.

improvement.justification: ImageNet and label-noise tests strengthen empirical validation, while the revised explanation and code-access information improve clarity and reproducibility guidance. These benefits are tempered by removed CIFAR comparisons and reporting inconsistencies: all-label ImageNet VI+MI is 64.5 ± 0.3 in Table 1 but 63.5 ± 0.4 in Table 5a, alongside conflicting seed and pretraining statements. The additional evidence supports a positive but limited net improvement.
